  (`CertificateParams::new`). The substance stands, and this plan does
  not reissue the certificate.

## The record

No change. A browser is a `PairedDevice` in `devices.json`
(`src/ports/remote.rs:96-107`, an unversioned `Vec`). The page sends
its name as `/pair`'s `device_name`. `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 16
(`src/core/model.rs:12`) and `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 1
(`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). The certificate in `identity.json` is
untouched. Decision 6: there is no `kind` field, because the name
("Safari on iPhone") is enough to list and revoke a device. If the
owner wants a browser marked as one, it becomes an additive
`#[serde(default)]` field in an unversioned file.

## The signals

Nothing new. The page hears the existing `hello`, `changed`, `removed`,
`watching` and `resync_required` frames. The only new input is the
token read from `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (see Actions).

## The actions and effects

There is no new `AppAction` or `Effect`. The only frame-side addition is
one read-only endpoint. Everything else is in the listener, the UI's
payload and the page.

**1. Trust: the click-through is the trust step.** On the first visit
the owner sees a certificate warning and accepts it. The device then
trusts that certificate at that address. The paired-devices dialog says
so (see UI).

- Why: Chrome remembers a bypass by host and certificate and applies it
  to later requests, WebSocket included (Settled, Chrome lines).
  Firefox pins the exception to host:port, and the same origin
  guarantees that (Settled). Installing the certificate instead would
  need a reissue with an IP SAN, `serverAuth` and at most 825 days, plus
  the iOS full-trust toggle (Settled, Apple lines). Whether iOS even
  offers that toggle for a non-CA leaf is Unresolved, and the
  certificate would need reissuing every time the address changes.
- What it buys: the page's key check refuses to send the code to a
  genuine host whose key differs.
- What it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not our page,
  and the code in the URL reaches whatever host the owner clicked
  through to.
- What rests on Unresolved: whether Safari honours the exception for
  `wss://` (WebKit bug 41419, still NEW). This is the question the plan
  turns on most. The page therefore ships its own fallback. If the
  socket fails twice before `hello`, the page polls `projects` and each
  project's `sessions` every 5 s. It refetches the open view's content
  only when that session's `last_activity_ms` or `last_stop_at_ms`
  moves, never on a timer, so polling never parses a transcript for
  nothing. The header says "Live updates unavailable; refreshing every
  5 s". The fallback is built now because the answer only comes from
  the owner's device run at acceptance.
- If `fetch` fails as well after the click-through (also Unresolved),
  the install path above is what a follow-up issue builds.

**2. Token transport: the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` subprotocol, with the
token in `localStorage`.**

- REST is unchanged. `fetch` sets `Authorization: Bearer` itself, so
  the host keeps reading the bearer header for every client.
- For the socket, the page calls
  `new WebSocket(url, ["switchboard.v1", "bearer." + token])`.
- `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444-513`): when `upgrade` is
  set and there is no `Authorization` header, it splits
  `sec-websocket-protocol` on commas. If `switchboard.v1` is among the
  values, the `bearer.`-prefixed value becomes `bearer` and a new field
  `subprotocol: Option<String>` is set to `switchboard.v1`. The token
  stays in the one field that is never logged.
- `connection` clones `subprotocol` next to `upgrade_key` (`:798`).
  `respond_upgrade` (`:519-527`) takes it and writes
  `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: switchboard.v1`. It echoes the name, never
  the token. The browser fails the handshake without that echo
  (Settled). The token's characters are all `tchar` (Settled).
- A native client offers no subprotocol and gets no echo, so its path
  is unchanged.
- `RemoteRequest` is not in the shared contract (Settled), and
  `read_request` is its only constructor (Settled).
- Why not the cookie:
  - It goes to every port on the host (Settled).
  - It needs an `Origin` check against cross-site WebSocket hijacking.
  - It rests on three Unresolved lines: `SameSite=Strict` on `wss`, a
    `Secure` cookie on an IP host after a click-through, and
    secure-context status.
- What the subprotocol rests on, all Settled: `localStorage` is per
  origin, so two instances on two ports never share a token, and it
  does not need a secure context.
- The cost: any script on the origin can read `localStorage`. The
  origin serves only our three files under a CSP with
  `script-src 'self'`, and the page never turns data into markup (a
  test checks this).
- There is no `Origin` check. A browser never attaches a bearer token
  or a subprotocol by itself, so a cross-site page has nothing to
  replay. This answers the For the owner line "Check `Origin`" the way
  that line says the subprotocol choice implies. If the owner wants the
  check anyway, `read_request` keeps `Origin` and `Host`, and the
  upgrade and every POST refuse an `Origin` other than
  `https://<Host>`.
- Op ids come from `crypto.getRandomValues` (16 bytes as hex, within
  `OP_CAP` = 64), never from `randomUUID` (Settled: it does not need a
  secure context).

**3. One QR: a URL.**

- The payload is
  `https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
- It is built by a pure function,
  `core::remote::invite_url(identity, code, ip, port)`. The UI calls it
  in place of the `json!` at `src/ui/remote.rs:160-166`.
- The host part is `remote::local_address()`, which is always IPv4, so
  there are no brackets (Settled). When there is no address it falls
  back to `127.0.0.1`. That is honest for a loopback-only listen.
- The IP was chosen over `.local` because whether iOS resolves
  `<name>.local`, and which name the Mac advertises, are both
  Unresolved. If the owner's run favours `.local`, the host part
  becomes the `default_server_name()` name, a one-line change at the
  call site. Until then, a new IP means a new warning in Chrome.
- The native text path takes the URL too. `PairingInvite.parse`
  (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:113-116`) tries
  `URLComponents` first: `https` scheme, `code`, `key`, `id`, and the
  host and port as the one entry in `addresses`. That is enough, since
  only the first address is used (Settled: Swift line).
- It falls back to the JSON as today, so a pasted old invite and the
  fixtures keep working. `switchboard-remote pair` (`main.swift:111`)
  and `BrowserView` (`:106`, `:883`) call `parse` and change only in
  the usage text (`main.swift:12`).

**4. Static paths.**

- `src/adapters/web.rs` holds the embedded files: `PAGE`, an array of
  `PageFile { path, content_type, body }` built with
  `include_str!("../../web/…")`, and `CSP`.
- The three paths:
  - `/`: `index.html`, `text/html; charset=utf-8`
  - `/app.js`: `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`
  - `/app.css`: `text/css; charset=utf-8`
- A query on `/` is ignored and never logged. Nothing on the connection
  thread logs a request.
- In `connection` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:770`), right after
  `read_request` and before the rate-window check (`:788`), a path
  outside `/api/v1/` is answered there:
  - a `GET` of a page file gets `respond_page`, a new writer beside
    `respond` (`:530-552`), so `RemoteReply` and its 30 literals are
    untouched;
  - anything else gets `respond(404, error_body("not_found", "no such
    endpoint"))`;
  - then `return Ok(())`.
- Headers on a page file:
  - `Content-Type` as above;
  - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
    style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; base-uri
    'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`;
  - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`;
  - `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`;
  - `Cache-Control: no-store`, so an updated host never runs an old
    script against a new API;
  - `Connection: close`.
- `index.html` has no inline script or style:
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/app.css">` and
  `<script src="/app.js" defer>`.
- Not in the facts file and unverified here: CSP Level 3 counts a
  same-host `wss:` as `'self'`. The owner's run checks the console for a
  CSP violation on the socket. If Safari reports one, `read_request`
  keeps `Host` and `connect-src` adds `wss://<Host>` per response.
- Pool and rate: a page load is unauthenticated, so it counts against
  the pool of 4 like any stranger. `Connection: close` frees each slot
  as soon as its file is written. The files get no rate window: they
  cost one write of compile-time bytes on the connection's own thread,
  and the pool already bounds a stranger. `/info` keeps its 60 a minute,
  and the page calls it once per load.
- How many connections iOS Safari opens, and whether the warning's
  failed handshake holds a slot, are Unresolved. Fallback: if the
  owner's run shows loads dropped at accept, raise
  `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` (`:567`) from 4 to 8 and amend §4.1.
- §5's rule becomes: "Require pairing before anything but `/info`,
  `/pair` and the page's three files, which are the same bytes for
  everyone and carry no state."

**5. `GET /api/v1/device` (read scope).**

- A new arm in `serve_remote` after `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3033`).
- It answers in the envelope with
  `{device_id, name, scope, server_id, server_name}`, where
  `authenticated` is true.
- The page reads it at load and after any `403 scope`, so a scope
  changed in the dialog shows on the device's next request.
- Spec §4.3 lists it. There is no `info` capability for it: the page
  ships with the host, and the Swift client does not use it yet.
- This rests on the For the owner line "Scope in the header". The
  fallback is the `/pair` reply's scope, flipped to read on a 403
  `scope`.

## The UI

**Host dialog** (`src/ui/remote.rs`):

- The QR code and "Copy invite" carry the URL. The hover text becomes
  "The QR code's link: a phone's camera opens it; a client takes it
  pasted".
- Under "Paired devices", one new `meta_text` line: "A browser pairs
  from the QR code's link. Its first visit shows a certificate warning:
  accepting it is what trusts this Mac on that device, so accept it only
  on your own network, from a code this window shows. The page checks
  the host's key against the link, which catches a different host, not
  an impostor."

**The page** (`web/index.html`, `web/app.js`, `web/app.css`):

- Plain DOM. Text goes through `textContent`. There is no framework and
  no build step.
- Load:
  1. If the URL has a query, read it, then
     `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")` before anything else.
  2. `GET /api/v1/info`.
- With a code: if `key` or `id` differs from `/info`, the page says
  "This is not the host whose code was scanned. Nothing was sent."
  Otherwise it posts `/api/v1/pair {code, device_name, spki_sha256:
  key}`. The `device_name` is "<browser> on <device>" from
  `navigator.userAgent`, with an iPad that reports a Mac told apart by
  `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1`. On success it stores
  `{server_id, spki_sha256, token, device_id}` in `localStorage`, every
  access in try/catch. `pairing_closed` and `wrong_code` are said in
  words.
- With a stored token:
  - `/info`'s key differs: "This host's identity changed. Pair again."
    The token is dropped and nothing is sent.
  - The `server_id` differs: "Another host answers at this address.
    Pair again."
  - Otherwise `GET device`. A 401 means "This device was revoked on the
    host. Pair again."
- With neither a code nor a token: "Not paired. On the Mac, open
  Settings → Remote devices…, allow devices on the local network, allow
  pairing, and scan the code with this device's camera."
- Header: `server_name`, the device's name and scope, and the live or
  polling state.
- List, §4.4's order:
  1. Open the socket and wait for `hello`.
  2. Fetch `projects`, then each project's `sessions`.
  3. Reconcile the buffered events by revision.
- Projects with a waiting session come first. Within a project,
  waiting sessions come first and are marked. Each row shows the name,
  kind, card word, `waiting_reason`, and the excerpt from the first
  departure.
- `changed session` refetches that session, plus its `last-response`
  if it is a waiting Claude Code session. `changed sessions` and
  `changed projects` refetch the collection. `removed` drops the row.
  `resync_required` reconnects and refetches everything.
- Session view: `last-response` for `kind: claude`, `screen?lines=60`
  otherwise.
  - It sends `watch` for its one key, fetches after `watching`, and
    refetches on `changed` for that key and every 30 s (§4.4). It sends
    `unwatch` on leaving.
  - The whole page holds at most one watched key, so it cannot crowd
    the headset out of the 128 (Settled: watch-set line).
- Reply box: shown only under `control`. It posts
  `sessions/{id}/send {op, text}`. On a timeout or a network error it
  asks `ops/{op}` before offering a retry (§4.5). A 403 `scope`
  re-reads `device` and hides the box.
- A closed socket reconnects with backoff. A 401 on the upgrade or on
  any request shows the revoked state, which is how revocation reaches
  the page at once: revocation closes the socket
  (`tests/remote.rs:2892`).
- All endpoint paths are in one `const API` block at the top of
  `app.js`, which the test reads.

I've written the plan to `/Users/sbgragent/Library/Application Support/Dispatch/tickets/b96d09c6/plan/1/repo/plan.md`. File and line references are checked against this worktree at 7fe8949.

**The six decisions:**
1. **Trust:** accepting the certificate warning is the trust step, and the paired-devices dialog says so. The plan leans hardest on an open question: whether Safari keeps that acceptance for the events WebSocket. So the page ships a fallback now. If the socket fails, it polls the session lists every 5 s and refetches content only when a session's activity time moves. If `fetch` also fails, installing the certificate is a follow-up issue.
2. **Token on the WebSocket:** the page passes it as a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value (`switchboard.v1` plus `bearer.<token>`), and the host echoes only the name. The token lives in `localStorage`; REST calls keep the bearer header, so the native clients are untouched. I chose this over the cookie because a cookie goes to every port on the Mac, would need an `Origin` check, and depends on three unanswered browser questions.
3. **One QR code:** it carries the URL, using the IP address. `PairingInvite.parse` in the Swift client tries the URL first and falls back to the JSON.
4. **Static paths:** `/`, `/app.js` and `/app.css` are answered on the connection thread, never by the frame. Each reply carries a fixed CSP, `no-store`, `nosniff` and `no-referrer`, then closes the connection so it frees its slot in the pool of 4. Any other path outside `/api/v1/` gets the same `404 not_found` as today, also from the connection thread. If the phone run shows page loads being dropped at accept, the fallback is raising that pool from 4 to 8.
5. **Testing:** the host side gets four new integration tests in `tests/remote.rs`, a unit test, a core test, an updated UI test and a Swift test. The page's own JavaScript has no test runner, so it is checked by hand at acceptance.

`:16`/`:18`/`:19` (key and params at `:101`/`:102`, not `:105`/`:106`)
is right.

project's `.claude/` or `.switchboard/`. No serialized type changes, so
no schema bump is needed (`devices.json` is untouched). `RemoteRequest`
gaining a field is outside the contract (facts `:15`).

   (line 322-323) that the whole page holds at most one watched key, so
   it "cannot crowd the headset out of the 128". The watch set is not
   only keys asked for with `watch`. It is "every content key any
   subscriber has asked to watch, **plus every content key read in the
   last minute**" (`docs/remote-client.md:254`; facts `:24` and `:69`,
   "the page fetches `last-response` per session … and spends
   watch-set slots").

   `last-response` on every waiting Claude Code row (lines 29-31,
   311-314), reads one content key per waiting session. Those reads
   happen again on every `changed session`, and on every
   `last_activity_ms` move while polling. Each read puts its key in the
   set for a minute.

   most N waiting rows (N well under 128), fetched only on load and on
   that session's `changed`, or accept it in words, citing `:254` and
   facts `:69`. Then correct the "at most one watched key" sentence and
   the matching §5 / design-status text.

   (lines 328-331) says "a 401 on the upgrade … shows the revoked
   state". It also says the poll fallback starts when "the socket fails
   twice before `hello`" (lines 115-116). Settled against the primary
   source: the WHATWG WebSockets standard, §2.2, says a non-101
   response must "fail the WebSocket connection". §4 says user agents
   "must not convey any failure information to scripts in a way that
   would allow a script to distinguish" a server that did not complete
   the handshake from other failures. The page sees `error` and then
   `close` with code 1006, and no status
   (https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/).

   the click-through for `wss` (facts `:49`), and a host that is down
   or relaunching. With the plan as written:

     authenticated `fetch` (`GET device`) before it reconnects or
     counts a failure. A 401 there is the revoked state. A network
     error means the host is unreachable: back off and do not count a
     failure. A 200 counts one failure toward the fallback.
   - In polling mode, retry the socket now and then (for example every
     minute), so a page that fell back after a transient failure
     returns to live.
   - Reword lines 328-331 and step 6 of the end-to-end test to match.
     Revocation closes the socket (`tests/remote.rs:2892`), and the
     next `GET device` is what says "revoked".

   page files.** The plan has non-page paths answered with
   `respond(404, …)` "then a close" (lines 214-216). Its test expects
   `/favicon.ico` and `POST /` to answer "the same way" as the page
   files, a list that includes `Connection: close` (lines 347-350).
   `respond` writes `Connection: keep-alive`
   (`src/adapters/remote.rs:545`), so the reply would claim keep-alive
   and then drop the connection. That works, but the plan contradicts
   itself and the test as written would fail.

   Fix: write the 404 with a `Connection: close` head. That can be
   `respond_page`'s writer with the JSON content type, or a `close`
   flag on a private helper. Alternatively, state that the 404 keeps
   `respond`'s head, and drop it from the "same way" assertion.

   requires, and the plan does not say so.** Today a non-API path is
   refused through `refuse`, which logs

   thread logs a request" (line 207) silently removes that log for

   path only, never the query, since `/?code=` carries the code. Or
   amend `:318` and §4.1 to say that non-API paths are answered unlogged
   and why: the page's query holds a pairing code.

   settled, and should be cited.** The plan (lines 230-233) leaves it as
   "Not in the facts file and unverified here", with a fallback. The
   primary source settles the spec side. CSP Level 3 §6.7.2.8 ("Does url

   branch, matches when the hosts match, the ports match or are

   2.

   (https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=201591,
   https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=235873). The bug does not

     cite this instead: the HTML standard's `WindowLocalStorage` IDL
     carries no `[SecureContext]`

     also needs a stated behaviour for it, for example "this browser

1	# Plan: a web control surface on the remote port (#230)
2	
3	The remote port also serves a page: three files compiled into the
4	binary and answered by the connection thread. The page pairs from a
5	URL in the pairing window's QR code and then speaks the protocol the
6	headset speaks. The browser's click-through of the certificate warning
7	is the trust step. The token stays in the page's `localStorage`. The
8	page sends it as the bearer header on `fetch` and as a
9	`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value on the events socket. One commit. The
10	app runs before and after it. Line numbers are from this worktree at
11	7fe8949.
12	
13	## Where this departs from the issue
14	
15	- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused."** True, but the refusal
16	  happens on the frame (`src/app.rs:3023-3025`), after the request has
17	  already taken a slot in the inbox of 64. The plan answers every path
18	  outside `/api/v1/` on the connection thread instead: the page's three
19	  files, or the same `404 not_found` body as today, then a close. The
20	  frame never sees such a request. The prefix arm in `serve_remote`
21	  stays as a guard.
22	- **"The one-line excerpt the card shows."** The wire does not carry
23	  it. The record has no `last_message`, and the card computes the
24	  excerpt in the UI from the conversation cache or the pane caption
25	  (Settled: "The record carries no `last_message`";

27	  `SessionView` would put content on a metadata view that skips the

29	  only"). In this cut, a waiting Claude Code session's row shows the
30	  first line of its `last-response`, cut the way `agent_excerpt` cuts
31	  it (160 characters). Every other row shows the card's word and
32	  `waiting_reason`. This rests on the For the owner line "Card
33	  excerpt". If the owner wants every row excerpted, a later issue adds
34	  an `excerpt` field to `SessionView`, computed in `app.rs` through
35	  redaction, with a fixture change on both sides.
36	- **"The device's scope … in the header."** No endpoint tells a device
37	  its scope after pairing. `/info` is unauthenticated
38	  (`src/app.rs:3568-3600`). The plan adds `GET /api/v1/device` (see
39	  Actions).
40	- **"'Revoked' said plainly."** The host cannot say it. Both refusals
41	  in `authenticate` have the code `unauthorized`
42	  (`src/app.rs:3127-3153`). A revoked token's hash is gone from
43	  `devices.json` (`RevokeDevice`, `src/core/remote.rs:86-92`), so the
44	  host cannot tell a revoked token from one it never issued. The page
45	  infers it instead: it holds a token for this `server_id`, `/info`
46	  still shows the same key, and the answer is 401. That page reads
47	  "This device was revoked on the host." This rests on the For the
48	  owner line "Revoked versus never paired". Recording revoked hashes
49	  would be new host state, and nothing in this cut needs it.
50	- **"Compares the key in the URL with the one `/info` presents."** This
51	  proves only what `/info` claims. Whether a page can read its own
52	  connection's certificate is Unresolved. The host checks only the
53	  `spki_sha256` in the body (Settled, §5 relay line;
54	  `src/app.rs:3639-3647`). The check catches a genuine page talking to
55	  the wrong genuine host. It does not catch an impostor that serves its
56	  own page. The spec's relay sentence (`docs/remote-client.md:309`) is
57	  amended to say so for browsers.
58	- **"The code never stays in the address bar or the history."**
59	  `replaceState` rewrites only the session-history entry. Whether the
60	  URL reaches Safari's global history or iCloud Tabs first is
61	  Unresolved. What actually protects the code is that it is single use
62	  and lasts five minutes (Settled: "A code is single use"). The spec
63	  says that, and treats `replaceState` as tidying, not as the
64	  guarantee.
65	- **Facts correction.** The settled line on reissuing the certificate
66	  cites `src/adapters/remote.rs:105-106` for the key and the params.
67	  In the tree they are at `:101` (`KeyPair::generate`) and `:102`
68	  (`CertificateParams::new`). The substance stands, and this plan does
69	  not reissue the certificate.
70	
71	## The record
72	
73	No change. A browser is a `PairedDevice` in `devices.json`
74	(`src/ports/remote.rs:96-107`, an unversioned `Vec`). The page sends
75	its name as `/pair`'s `device_name`. `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 16
76	(`src/core/model.rs:12`) and `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 1
77	(`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). The certificate in `identity.json` is
78	untouched. Decision 6: there is no `kind` field, because the name
79	("Safari on iPhone") is enough to list and revoke a device. If the
80	owner wants a browser marked as one, it becomes an additive
81	`#[serde(default)]` field in an unversioned file.
82	
83	## The signals
84	
85	Nothing new. The page hears the existing `hello`, `changed`, `removed`,
86	`watching` and `resync_required` frames. The only new input is the
87	token read from `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (see Actions).
88	
89	## The actions and effects
90	
91	There is no new `AppAction` or `Effect`. The only frame-side addition is
92	one read-only endpoint. Everything else is in the listener, the UI's
93	payload and the page.
94	
95	**1. Trust: the click-through is the trust step.** On the first visit
96	the owner sees a certificate warning and accepts it. The device then
97	trusts that certificate at that address. The paired-devices dialog says
98	so (see UI).
99	
100	- Why: Chrome remembers a bypass by host and certificate and applies it
101	  to later requests, WebSocket included (Settled, Chrome lines).
102	  Firefox pins the exception to host:port, and the same origin
103	  guarantees that (Settled). Installing the certificate instead would
104	  need a reissue with an IP SAN, `serverAuth` and at most 825 days, plus
105	  the iOS full-trust toggle (Settled, Apple lines). Whether iOS even
106	  offers that toggle for a non-CA leaf is Unresolved, and the
107	  certificate would need reissuing every time the address changes.
108	- What it buys: the page's key check refuses to send the code to a
109	  genuine host whose key differs.
110	- What it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not our page,
111	  and the code in the URL reaches whatever host the owner clicked
112	  through to.
113	- What rests on Unresolved: whether Safari honours the exception for
114	  `wss://` (WebKit bug 41419, still NEW). This is the question the plan
115	  turns on most. The page therefore ships its own fallback. If the
116	  socket fails twice before `hello`, the page polls `projects` and each
117	  project's `sessions` every 5 s. It refetches the open view's content
118	  only when that session's `last_activity_ms` or `last_stop_at_ms`
119	  moves, never on a timer, so polling never parses a transcript for
120	  nothing. The header says "Live updates unavailable; refreshing every
121	  5 s". The fallback is built now because the answer only comes from
122	  the owner's device run at acceptance.
123	- If `fetch` fails as well after the click-through (also Unresolved),
124	  the install path above is what a follow-up issue builds.
125	
126	**2. Token transport: the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` subprotocol, with the
127	token in `localStorage`.**
128	
129	- REST is unchanged. `fetch` sets `Authorization: Bearer` itself, so
130	  the host keeps reading the bearer header for every client.
131	- For the socket, the page calls
132	  `new WebSocket(url, ["switchboard.v1", "bearer." + token])`.
133	- `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444-513`): when `upgrade` is
134	  set and there is no `Authorization` header, it splits
135	  `sec-websocket-protocol` on commas. If `switchboard.v1` is among the
136	  values, the `bearer.`-prefixed value becomes `bearer` and a new field
137	  `subprotocol: Option<String>` is set to `switchboard.v1`. The token
138	  stays in the one field that is never logged.
139	- `connection` clones `subprotocol` next to `upgrade_key` (`:797`).
140	  `respond_upgrade` (`:519-527`) takes it and writes
141	  `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: switchboard.v1`. It echoes the name, never
142	  the token. The browser fails the handshake without that echo
143	  (Settled). The token's characters are all `tchar` (Settled).
144	- A native client offers no subprotocol and gets no echo, so its path
145	  is unchanged.
146	- `RemoteRequest` is not in the shared contract (Settled), and
147	  `read_request` is its only constructor (Settled).
148	- Why not the cookie:
149	  - It goes to every port on the host (Settled).
150	  - It needs an `Origin` check against cross-site WebSocket hijacking.
151	  - It rests on three Unresolved lines: `SameSite=Strict` on `wss`, a
152	    `Secure` cookie on an IP host after a click-through, and
153	    secure-context status.
154	- What the subprotocol rests on, all Settled: `localStorage` is per
155	  origin, so two instances on two ports never share a token, and it
156	  does not need a secure context.
157	- The cost: any script on the origin can read `localStorage`. The
158	  origin serves only our three files under a CSP with
159	  `script-src 'self'`, and the page never turns data into markup (a
160	  test checks this).
161	- There is no `Origin` check. A browser never attaches a bearer token
162	  or a subprotocol by itself, so a cross-site page has nothing to
163	  replay. This answers the For the owner line "Check `Origin`" the way
164	  that line says the subprotocol choice implies. If the owner wants the
165	  check anyway, `read_request` keeps `Origin` and `Host`, and the
166	  upgrade and every POST refuse an `Origin` other than
167	  `https://<Host>`.
168	- Op ids come from `crypto.getRandomValues` (16 bytes as hex, within
169	  `OP_CAP` = 64), never from `randomUUID` (Settled: it does not need a
170	  secure context).
171	
172	**3. One QR: a URL.**
173	
174	- The payload is
175	  `https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
176	- It is built by a pure function,
177	  `core::remote::invite_url(identity, code, ip, port)`. The UI calls it
178	  in place of the `json!` at `src/ui/remote.rs:160-166`.
179	- The host part is `remote::local_address()`, which is always IPv4, so
180	  there are no brackets (Settled). When there is no address it falls
181	  back to `127.0.0.1`. That is honest for a loopback-only listen.
182	- The IP was chosen over `.local` because whether iOS resolves
183	  `<name>.local`, and which name the Mac advertises, are both
184	  Unresolved. If the owner's run favours `.local`, the host part
185	  becomes the `default_server_name()` name, a one-line change at the
186	  call site. Until then, a new IP means a new warning in Chrome.
187	- The native text path takes the URL too. `PairingInvite.parse`
188	  (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:113-116`) tries
189	  `URLComponents` first: `https` scheme, `code`, `key`, `id`, and the
190	  host and port as the one entry in `addresses`. That is enough, since
191	  only the first address is used (Settled: Swift line).
192	- It falls back to the JSON as today, so a pasted old invite and the
193	  fixtures keep working. `switchboard-remote pair` (`main.swift:111`)
194	  and `BrowserView` (`:106`, `:883`) call `parse` and change only in
195	  the usage text (`main.swift:12`).
196	
197	**4. Static paths.**
198	
199	- `src/adapters/web.rs` holds the embedded files: `PAGE`, an array of
200	  `PageFile { path, content_type, body }` built with
201	  `include_str!("../../web/…")`, and `CSP`.
202	- The three paths:
203	  - `/`: `index.html`, `text/html; charset=utf-8`
204	  - `/app.js`: `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`
205	  - `/app.css`: `text/css; charset=utf-8`
206	- A query on `/` is ignored and never logged. Nothing on the connection
207	  thread logs a request.
208	- In `connection` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:770`), right after
209	  `read_request` and before the rate-window check (`:788`), a path
210	  outside `/api/v1/` is answered there:
211	  - a `GET` of a page file gets `respond_page`, a new writer beside
212	    `respond` (`:530-552`), so `RemoteReply` and its 30 literals are
213	    untouched;
214	  - anything else gets `respond(404, error_body("not_found", "no such
215	    endpoint"))`;
216	  - then `return Ok(())`.
217	- Headers on a page file:
218	  - `Content-Type` as above;
219	  - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
220	    style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; base-uri
221	    'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`;
222	  - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`;
223	  - `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`;
224	  - `Cache-Control: no-store`, so an updated host never runs an old
225	    script against a new API;
226	  - `Connection: close`.
227	- `index.html` has no inline script or style:
228	  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/app.css">` and
229	  `<script src="/app.js" defer>`.
230	- Not in the facts file and unverified here: CSP Level 3 counts a
231	  same-host `wss:` as `'self'`. The owner's run checks the console for a
232	  CSP violation on the socket. If Safari reports one, `read_request`
233	  keeps `Host` and `connect-src` adds `wss://<Host>` per response.
234	- Pool and rate: a page load is unauthenticated, so it counts against
235	  the pool of 4 like any stranger. `Connection: close` frees each slot
236	  as soon as its file is written. The files get no rate window: they
237	  cost one write of compile-time bytes on the connection's own thread,
238	  and the pool already bounds a stranger. `/info` keeps its 60 a minute,
239	  and the page calls it once per load.
240	- How many connections iOS Safari opens, and whether the warning's
241	  failed handshake holds a slot, are Unresolved. Fallback: if the
242	  owner's run shows loads dropped at accept, raise
243	  `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` (`:567`) from 4 to 8 and amend §4.1.
244	- §5's rule becomes: "Require pairing before anything but `/info`,
245	  `/pair` and the page's three files, which are the same bytes for
246	  everyone and carry no state."
247	
248	**5. `GET /api/v1/device` (read scope).**
249	
250	- A new arm in `serve_remote` after `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3033`).
251	- It answers in the envelope with
252	  `{device_id, name, scope, server_id, server_name}`, where
253	  `authenticated` is true.
254	- The page reads it at load and after any `403 scope`, so a scope
255	  changed in the dialog shows on the device's next request.
256	- Spec §4.3 lists it. There is no `info` capability for it: the page
257	  ships with the host, and the Swift client does not use it yet.
258	- This rests on the For the owner line "Scope in the header". The
259	  fallback is the `/pair` reply's scope, flipped to read on a 403
260	  `scope`.
261	
262	## The UI
263	
264	**Host dialog** (`src/ui/remote.rs`):
265	
266	- The QR code and "Copy invite" carry the URL. The hover text becomes
267	  "The QR code's link: a phone's camera opens it; a client takes it
268	  pasted".
269	- Under "Paired devices", one new `meta_text` line: "A browser pairs
270	  from the QR code's link. Its first visit shows a certificate warning:
271	  accepting it is what trusts this Mac on that device, so accept it only
272	  on your own network, from a code this window shows. The page checks
273	  the host's key against the link, which catches a different host, not
274	  an impostor."
275	
276	**The page** (`web/index.html`, `web/app.js`, `web/app.css`):
277	
278	- Plain DOM. Text goes through `textContent`. There is no framework and
279	  no build step.
280	- Load:
281	  1. If the URL has a query, read it, then
282	     `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")` before anything else.
283	  2. `GET /api/v1/info`.
284	- With a code: if `key` or `id` differs from `/info`, the page says
285	  "This is not the host whose code was scanned. Nothing was sent."
286	  Otherwise it posts `/api/v1/pair {code, device_name, spki_sha256:
287	  key}`. The `device_name` is "<browser> on <device>" from
288	  `navigator.userAgent`, with an iPad that reports a Mac told apart by
289	  `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1`. On success it stores
290	  `{server_id, spki_sha256, token, device_id}` in `localStorage`, every
291	  access in try/catch. `pairing_closed` and `wrong_code` are said in
292	  words.
293	- With a stored token:
294	  - `/info`'s key differs: "This host's identity changed. Pair again."
295	    The token is dropped and nothing is sent.
296	  - The `server_id` differs: "Another host answers at this address.
297	    Pair again."
298	  - Otherwise `GET device`. A 401 means "This device was revoked on the
299	    host. Pair again."
300	- With neither a code nor a token: "Not paired. On the Mac, open
301	  Settings → Remote devices…, allow devices on the local network, allow
302	  pairing, and scan the code with this device's camera."
303	- Header: `server_name`, the device's name and scope, and the live or
304	  polling state.
305	- List, §4.4's order:
306	  1. Open the socket and wait for `hello`.
307	  2. Fetch `projects`, then each project's `sessions`.
308	  3. Reconcile the buffered events by revision.
309	- Projects with a waiting session come first. Within a project,
310	  waiting sessions come first and are marked. Each row shows the name,
311	  kind, card word, `waiting_reason`, and the excerpt from the first
312	  departure.
313	- `changed session` refetches that session, plus its `last-response`
314	  if it is a waiting Claude Code session. `changed sessions` and
315	  `changed projects` refetch the collection. `removed` drops the row.
316	  `resync_required` reconnects and refetches everything.
317	- Session view: `last-response` for `kind: claude`, `screen?lines=60`
318	  otherwise.
319	  - It sends `watch` for its one key, fetches after `watching`, and
320	    refetches on `changed` for that key and every 30 s (§4.4). It sends
321	    `unwatch` on leaving.
322	  - The whole page holds at most one watched key, so it cannot crowd
323	    the headset out of the 128 (Settled: watch-set line).
324	- Reply box: shown only under `control`. It posts
325	  `sessions/{id}/send {op, text}`. On a timeout or a network error it
326	  asks `ops/{op}` before offering a retry (§4.5). A 403 `scope`
327	  re-reads `device` and hides the box.
328	- A closed socket reconnects with backoff. A 401 on the upgrade or on
329	  any request shows the revoked state, which is how revocation reaches
330	  the page at once: revocation closes the socket
331	  (`tests/remote.rs:2892`).
332	- All endpoint paths are in one `const API` block at the top of
333	  `app.js`, which the test reads.
334	
335	## The tests
336	
337	The page's logic has no JS harness in the tree, and the issue rules out
338	adding one (For the owner, "Page logic untested by CI"). The host side
339	is tested here, and the page is checked by hand at acceptance.
340	
341	- **`tests/remote.rs`.** Add `http_with`, which sends extra headers and
342	  returns `(status, headers, body)`. `http` (`:245`) becomes a wrapper.
343	  - `the_page_is_served_by_the_connection_thread_with_its_headers`:
344	    `/`, `/?code=X&key=Y&id=Z`, `/app.js` and `/app.css` are requested
345	    through `http_with` with no `serve_pending`. A reply that arrives
346	    shows the frame was never asked.
347	    - Each answers 200 with `web::PAGE`'s bytes and content type, the
348	      exact `web::CSP`, `nosniff`, `no-referrer`, `no-store` and
349	      `Connection: close`.
350	    - `/favicon.ico` and `POST /` answer 404 `not_found` the same way.
351	    - The existing `/other` check (`:465`) still passes.
352	  - `the_page_references_only_what_the_host_serves`:
353	    - every `src=` and `href=` in `index.html` is a `PAGE` path, and no
354	      file contains `http:`, `https:` or `//` in a reference;
355	    - every `/api/v1/` path in `app.js`'s `API` block is requested with
356	      a paired token, with `${…}` after `sessions/` and `projects/`
357	      replaced by `seed`'s ids. None answers 404 `not_found`, and the
358	      events path upgrades.
359	  - `the_page_writes_no_markup_from_data`: `app.js` has no `innerHTML`,
360	    `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write`, `eval(` or
361	    `new Function`.
362	  - `a_browser_pairs_and_subscribes_with_its_token_as_a_subprotocol`,
363	    end to end:
364	    1. `GET /`, then `info`, then `pair` with
365	       `device_name: "Safari on iPhone"`; the device is listed under
366	       that name.
367	    2. `GET device` gives the name and scope.
368	    3. Subscribe through a new `subscribe_with_protocol`, which sends
369	       `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: switchboard.v1, bearer.<token>` and no
370	       `Authorization`. The 101 carries `switchboard.v1`, which
371	       tungstenite checks, and `hello` arrives.
372	    4. A session that turns waiting sends its `changed`.
373	    5. A `send` under `control` reaches the fake host.
374	    6. Revoke closes the socket, and the next `GET device` is 401.
375	  - `a_subprotocol_token_needs_the_switchboard_name`: `bearer.<token>`
376	    alone is 401. The existing `subscribe_at` (`:1960`) still upgrades
377	    with no protocol echoed.
378	- **`src/adapters/remote.rs` unit test**, beside
379	  `a_request_reads_with_its_query_bearer_and_body` (`:1045`):
380	  `a_request_takes_its_bearer_from_the_websocket_protocol`. A header
381	  bearer wins. Protocols without `switchboard.v1` leave `bearer` empty.
382	- **`src/core/tests.rs`:** `invite_url_carries_the_code_key_and_id`,
383	  which checks the exact string for a fixed identity, code, IPv4 and
384	  port.
385	- **`tests/ui.rs`:** `remote_devices_dialog_opens_pairing_and_revokes_a_device`
386	  (`:7424`) parses the copied invite as a URL instead of JSON
387	  (`:7486-7492`): `https`, `code`, `key` equal to the identity's key,
388	  `id`. It also finds the browser trust line by label.
389	- **Swift** (`client/Tests/SwitchboardClientCoreTests/PairingTests.swift`):
390	  a URL invite parses to one address, and the JSON still parses. Run
391	  with `(cd client && swift test)`. It is not in CI or the hook.
392	- Fixtures do not change: no view changed shape.
393	- Acceptance by hand, recorded in the design status bullet:
394	  1. Run an instance on a test data dir with script lines
395	     `remote-listen lan <port>` and `pairing <code>`.
396	  2. Scan with an iPhone and accept the warning.
397	  3. Note whether the page is live or polling, and whether the console
398	     shows a CSP violation.
399	  4. Start a session waiting and watch it move to the top.
400	  5. Send a reply.
401	  6. Revoke the phone and see the page say so.
402	
403	## Docs
404	
405	- **`docs/remote-client.md`:**
406	  - §4.1: the connection thread answers the page and every non-API
407	    path, with `Connection: close` and no rate window.
408	  - §4.3: add rows for the three page paths and `GET /api/v1/device`.
409	  - §5:
410	    - the rule at `:306`;
411	    - the QR as a URL at `:309`;
412	    - the relay sentence at `:309`, which holds only for a client that
413	      pins;
414	    - the click-through as a browser's trust step, and the single-use
415	      code as the guarantee against a code left in history;
416	    - the token at `:312`: a bearer header, or a browser's
417	      `switchboard.v1` / `bearer.<token>` subprotocol pair on the
418	      events socket, never a URL;
419	    - a browser keeps its token in `localStorage` and pins nothing.
420	- **`docs/design.md`:** a bullet "**The page (#230).**" before "Known
421	  gaps at the first merge" (`:3573`). It says what is built, the poll
422	  fallback, the owner's device result, and the gaps: excerpts only for
423	  waiting Claude Code sessions, no tickets, no conversation beyond the
424	  last response.
425	- **`README.md`:**
426	  - Layout lines for `src/adapters/web.rs` and `web/`;
427	  - the `remote.rs` listener line (`:383`) gains "the page's files and
428	    any non-API path answered on the connection thread";
429	  - the `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT` dev-aid text (`:276-279`): "Copy
430	    invite" copies the link, which a browser opens and which
431	    `switchboard-remote pair "$(pbpaste)"` takes.
432	- **`client/README.md`:** the `pair` usage line.
433	- **`CHANGELOG.md`**, under Unreleased: "A browser on the local network
434	  can pair from the pairing window's QR code and list sessions, read
435	  the last response or screen, and send a reply."
436	
437	No spike directory: the one risky mechanism is browser behaviour, which
438	only the owner's device can answer. The page ships with its own
439	fallback either way, and the design status records the run.
440	
441	## Commit
442	
443	`The remote port serves a browser page that pairs from the QR code's link`
444	
445	Contract additions (none in `src/core/model.rs`, `src/core/action.rs` or
446	`src/ports/`):
447	
448	- `adapters::remote::RemoteRequest::subprotocol: Option<String>`
449	  (adapter type, outside the contract)
450	- `adapters::web` (new module): `PageFile`, `PAGE`, `CSP`
451	- `core::remote::invite_url`
452	- Wire: `GET /`, `GET /app.js`, `GET /app.css` before pairing;
453	  `GET /api/v1/device` (read); the `switchboard.v1` and
454	  `bearer.<token>` WebSocket subprotocols
455	- Swift: `PairingInvite.parse` accepts the URL form

# Plan: a web control surface on the remote port (#230)

The remote port also serves a page: three files compiled into the
binary and answered by the connection thread. The page pairs from a
URL in the pairing window's QR code and then speaks the protocol the
headset speaks. The browser's click-through of the certificate warning
is the trust step. The token stays in the page's `localStorage`. The
page sends it as the bearer header on `fetch` and as a
`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value on the events socket. One commit. The
app runs before and after it. Line numbers are from this worktree at
7fe8949.

## Where this departs from the issue

- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused."** True, but the refusal
  happens on the frame (`src/app.rs:3023-3025`), after the request has
  already taken a slot in the inbox of 64. The plan answers every path
  outside `/api/v1/` on the connection thread instead: the page's three
  files, or the same `404 not_found` body as today, then a close. The
  frame never sees such a request. The prefix arm in `serve_remote`
  stays as a guard.
- **"The one-line excerpt the card shows."** The wire does not carry
  it. The record has no `last_message`, and the card computes the
  excerpt in the UI from the conversation cache or the pane caption
  (Settled: "The record carries no `last_message`";

## The record

No change. A browser is a `PairedDevice` in `devices.json`
(`src/ports/remote.rs:96-107`, an unversioned `Vec`). The page sends
its name as `/pair`'s `device_name`. `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 16
(`src/core/model.rs:12`) and `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 1
(`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). The certificate in `identity.json` is
untouched. Decision 6: there is no `kind` field, because the name
("Safari on iPhone") is enough to list and revoke a device. If the
owner wants a browser marked as one, it becomes an additive
`#[serde(default)]` field in an unversioned file.

## The signals

Nothing new. The page hears the existing `hello`, `changed`, `removed`,
`watching` and `resync_required` frames. The only new input is the
token read from `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (see Actions).

## The actions and effects

There is no new `AppAction` or `Effect`. The only frame-side addition is
one read-only endpoint. Everything else is in the listener, the UI's
payload and the page.

**1. Trust: the click-through is the trust step.** On the first visit
the owner sees a certificate warning and accepts it. The device then
trusts that certificate at that address. The paired-devices dialog says
so (see UI).

- Why: Chrome remembers a bypass by host and certificate and applies it
  to later requests, WebSocket included (Settled, Chrome lines).
  Firefox pins the exception to host:port, and the same origin
  guarantees that (Settled). Installing the certificate instead would
  need a reissue with an IP SAN, `serverAuth` and at most 825 days, plus
  the iOS full-trust toggle (Settled, Apple lines). Whether iOS even
  offers that toggle for a non-CA leaf is Unresolved, and the
  certificate would need reissuing every time the address changes.
- What it buys: the page's key check refuses to send the code to a
  genuine host whose key differs.
- What it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not our page,
  and the code in the URL reaches whatever host the owner clicked
  through to.
- What rests on Unresolved: whether Safari honours the exception for
  `wss://` (WebKit bug 41419, still NEW). This is the question the plan
  turns on most. The page therefore ships its own fallback. If the
  socket fails twice before `hello`, the page polls `projects` and each
  project's `sessions` every 5 s. It refetches the open view's content
  only when that session's `last_activity_ms` or `last_stop_at_ms`
  moves, never on a timer, so polling never parses a transcript for
  nothing. The header says "Live updates unavailable; refreshing every
  5 s". The fallback is built now because the answer only comes from
  the owner's device run at acceptance.
- If `fetch` fails as well after the click-through (also Unresolved),
  the install path above is what a follow-up issue builds.

**2. Token transport: the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` subprotocol, with the
token in `localStorage`.**

- REST is unchanged. `fetch` sets `Authorization: Bearer` itself, so
  the host keeps reading the bearer header for every client.
- For the socket, the page calls
  `new WebSocket(url, ["switchboard.v1", "bearer." + token])`.
- `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444-513`): when `upgrade` is
  set and there is no `Authorization` header, it splits
  `sec-websocket-protocol` on commas. If `switchboard.v1` is among the
  values, the `bearer.`-prefixed value becomes `bearer` and a new field
  `subprotocol: Option<String>` is set to `switchboard.v1`. The token
  stays in the one field that is never logged.
- `connection` clones `subprotocol` next to `upgrade_key` (`:797`).
  `respond_upgrade` (`:519-527`) takes it and writes
  `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: switchboard.v1`. It echoes the name, never
  the token. The browser fails the handshake without that echo
  (Settled). The token's characters are all `tchar` (Settled).
- A native client offers no subprotocol and gets no echo, so its path
  is unchanged.
- `RemoteRequest` is not in the shared contract (Settled), and
  `read_request` is its only constructor (Settled).
- Why not the cookie:
  - It goes to every port on the host (Settled).
  - It needs an `Origin` check against cross-site WebSocket hijacking.
  - It rests on three Unresolved lines: `SameSite=Strict` on `wss`, a
    `Secure` cookie on an IP host after a click-through, and
    secure-context status.
- What the subprotocol rests on, all Settled: `localStorage` is per
  origin, so two instances on two ports never share a token, and it
  does not need a secure context.
- The cost: any script on the origin can read `localStorage`. The
  origin serves only our three files under a CSP with
  `script-src 'self'`, and the page never turns data into markup (a
  test checks this).
- There is no `Origin` check. A browser never attaches a bearer token
  or a subprotocol by itself, so a cross-site page has nothing to
  replay. This answers the For the owner line "Check `Origin`" the way
  that line says the subprotocol choice implies. If the owner wants the
  check anyway, `read_request` keeps `Origin` and `Host`, and the
  upgrade and every POST refuse an `Origin` other than
  `https://<Host>`.
- Op ids come from `crypto.getRandomValues` (16 bytes as hex, within
  `OP_CAP` = 64), never from `randomUUID` (Settled: it does not need a
  secure context).

**3. One QR: a URL.**

- The payload is
  `https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
- It is built by a pure function,
  `core::remote::invite_url(identity, code, ip, port)`. The UI calls it
  in place of the `json!` at `src/ui/remote.rs:160-166`.
- The host part is `remote::local_address()`, which is always IPv4, so
  there are no brackets (Settled). When there is no address it falls
  back to `127.0.0.1`. That is honest for a loopback-only listen.
- The IP was chosen over `.local` because whether iOS resolves
  `<name>.local`, and which name the Mac advertises, are both
  Unresolved. If the owner's run favours `.local`, the host part
  becomes the `default_server_name()` name, a one-line change at the
  call site. Until then, a new IP means a new warning in Chrome.
- The native text path takes the URL too. `PairingInvite.parse`
  (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:113-116`) tries
  `URLComponents` first: `https` scheme, `code`, `key`, `id`, and the
  host and port as the one entry in `addresses`. That is enough, since
  only the first address is used (Settled: Swift line).
- It falls back to the JSON as today, so a pasted old invite and the
  fixtures keep working. `switchboard-remote pair` (`main.swift:111`)
  and `BrowserView` (`:106`, `:883`) call `parse` and change only in
  the usage text (`main.swift:12`).

**4. Static paths.**

- `src/adapters/web.rs` holds the embedded files: `PAGE`, an array of
  `PageFile { path, content_type, body }` built with
  `include_str!("../../web/…")`, and `CSP`.
- The three paths:
  - `/`: `index.html`, `text/html; charset=utf-8`
  - `/app.js`: `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`
  - `/app.css`: `text/css; charset=utf-8`
- A query on `/` is ignored and never logged. Nothing on the connection
  thread logs a request.
- In `connection` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:770`), right after
  `read_request` and before the rate-window check (`:788`), a path
  outside `/api/v1/` is answered there:
  - a `GET` of a page file gets `respond_page`, a new writer beside
    `respond` (`:530-552`), so `RemoteReply` and its 30 literals are
    untouched;
  - anything else gets `respond(404, error_body("not_found", "no such
    endpoint"))`;
  - then `return Ok(())`.
- Headers on a page file:
  - `Content-Type` as above;
  - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
    style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; base-uri
    'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`;
  - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`;
  - `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`;
  - `Cache-Control: no-store`, so an updated host never runs an old
    script against a new API;
  - `Connection: close`.
- `index.html` has no inline script or style:
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/app.css">` and
  `<script src="/app.js" defer>`.
- Not in the facts file and unverified here: CSP Level 3 counts a
  same-host `wss:` as `'self'`. The owner's run checks the console for a
  CSP violation on the socket. If Safari reports one, `read_request`
  keeps `Host` and `connect-src` adds `wss://<Host>` per response.
- Pool and rate: a page load is unauthenticated, so it counts against
  the pool of 4 like any stranger. `Connection: close` frees each slot
  as soon as its file is written. The files get no rate window: they
  cost one write of compile-time bytes on the connection's own thread,
  and the pool already bounds a stranger. `/info` keeps its 60 a minute,
  and the page calls it once per load.
- How many connections iOS Safari opens, and whether the warning's
  failed handshake holds a slot, are Unresolved. Fallback: if the
  owner's run shows loads dropped at accept, raise
  `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` (`:567`) from 4 to 8 and amend §4.1.
- §5's rule becomes: "Require pairing before anything but `/info`,
  `/pair` and the page's three files, which are the same bytes for
  everyone and carry no state."

**5. `GET /api/v1/device` (read scope).**

- A new arm in `serve_remote` after `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3033`).
- It answers in the envelope with
  `{device_id, name, scope, server_id, server_name}`, where
  `authenticated` is true.
- The page reads it at load and after any `403 scope`, so a scope
  changed in the dialog shows on the device's next request.
- Spec §4.3 lists it. There is no `info` capability for it: the page
  ships with the host, and the Swift client does not use it yet.
- This rests on the For the owner line "Scope in the header". The
  fallback is the `/pair` reply's scope, flipped to read on a 403
  `scope`.

## The UI

**Host dialog** (`src/ui/remote.rs`):

- The QR code and "Copy invite" carry the URL. The hover text becomes
  "The QR code's link: a phone's camera opens it; a client takes it
  pasted".
- Under "Paired devices", one new `meta_text` line: "A browser pairs
  from the QR code's link. Its first visit shows a certificate warning:
  accepting it is what trusts this Mac on that device, so accept it only
  on your own network, from a code this window shows. The page checks
  the host's key against the link, which catches a different host, not
  an impostor."

**The page** (`web/index.html`, `web/app.js`, `web/app.css`):

- Plain DOM. Text goes through `textContent`. There is no framework and
  no build step.
- Load:
  1. If the URL has a query, read it, then
     `history.replaceState(null, "", "/")` before anything else.
  2. `GET /api/v1/info`.
- With a code: if `key` or `id` differs from `/info`, the page says
  "This is not the host whose code was scanned. Nothing was sent."
  Otherwise it posts `/api/v1/pair {code, device_name, spki_sha256:
  key}`. The `device_name` is "<browser> on <device>" from
  `navigator.userAgent`, with an iPad that reports a Mac told apart by
  `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1`. On success it stores
  `{server_id, spki_sha256, token, device_id}` in `localStorage`, every
  access in try/catch. `pairing_closed` and `wrong_code` are said in
  words.
- With a stored token:
  - `/info`'s key differs: "This host's identity changed. Pair again."
    The token is dropped and nothing is sent.
  - The `server_id` differs: "Another host answers at this address.
    Pair again."
  - Otherwise `GET device`. A 401 means "This device was revoked on the
    host. Pair again."
- With neither a code nor a token: "Not paired. On the Mac, open
  Settings → Remote devices…, allow devices on the local network, allow
  pairing, and scan the code with this device's camera."
- Header: `server_name`, the device's name and scope, and the live or
  polling state.
- List, §4.4's order:
  1. Open the socket and wait for `hello`.
  2. Fetch `projects`, then each project's `sessions`.
  3. Reconcile the buffered events by revision.
- Projects with a waiting session come first. Within a project,
  waiting sessions come first and are marked. Each row shows the name,
  kind, card word, `waiting_reason`, and the excerpt from the first
  departure.
- `changed session` refetches that session, plus its `last-response`
  if it is a waiting Claude Code session. `changed sessions` and
  `changed projects` refetch the collection. `removed` drops the row.
  `resync_required` reconnects and refetches everything.
- Session view: `last-response` for `kind: claude`, `screen?lines=60`
  otherwise.
  - It sends `watch` for its one key, fetches after `watching`, and
    refetches on `changed` for that key and every 30 s (§4.4). It sends
    `unwatch` on leaving.
  - The whole page holds at most one watched key, so it cannot crowd
    the headset out of the 128 (Settled: watch-set line).
- Reply box: shown only under `control`. It posts
  `sessions/{id}/send {op, text}`. On a timeout or a network error it
  asks `ops/{op}` before offering a retry (§4.5). A 403 `scope`
  re-reads `device` and hides the box.
- A closed socket reconnects with backoff. A 401 on the upgrade or on
  any request shows the revoked state, which is how revocation reaches
  the page at once: revocation closes the socket
  (`tests/remote.rs:2892`).
- All endpoint paths are in one `const API` block at the top of
  `app.js`, which the test reads.

## The tests

The page's logic has no JS harness in the tree, and the issue rules out
adding one (For the owner, "Page logic untested by CI"). The host side
is tested here, and the page is checked by hand at acceptance.

- **`tests/remote.rs`.** Add `http_with`, which sends extra headers and
  returns `(status, headers, body)`. `http` (`:245`) becomes a wrapper.
  - `the_page_is_served_by_the_connection_thread_with_its_headers`:
    `/`, `/?code=X&key=Y&id=Z`, `/app.js` and `/app.css` are requested
    through `http_with` with no `serve_pending`. A reply that arrives
    shows the frame was never asked.
    - Each answers 200 with `web::PAGE`'s bytes and content type, the
      exact `web::CSP`, `nosniff`, `no-referrer`, `no-store` and
      `Connection: close`.
    - `/favicon.ico` and `POST /` answer 404 `not_found` the same way.
    - The existing `/other` check (`:465`) still passes.
  - `the_page_references_only_what_the_host_serves`:
    - every `src=` and `href=` in `index.html` is a `PAGE` path, and no
      file contains `http:`, `https:` or `//` in a reference;
    - every `/api/v1/` path in `app.js`'s `API` block is requested with
      a paired token, with `${…}` after `sessions/` and `projects/`
      replaced by `seed`'s ids. None answers 404 `not_found`, and the
      events path upgrades.
  - `the_page_writes_no_markup_from_data`: `app.js` has no `innerHTML`,
    `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write`, `eval(` or
    `new Function`.
  - `a_browser_pairs_and_subscribes_with_its_token_as_a_subprotocol`,
    end to end:
    1. `GET /`, then `info`, then `pair` with
       `device_name: "Safari on iPhone"`; the device is listed under
       that name.
    2. `GET device` gives the name and scope.
    3. Subscribe through a new `subscribe_with_protocol`, which sends
       `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: switchboard.v1, bearer.<token>` and no
       `Authorization`. The 101 carries `switchboard.v1`, which
       tungstenite checks, and `hello` arrives.
    4. A session that turns waiting sends its `changed`.
    5. A `send` under `control` reaches the fake host.
    6. Revoke closes the socket, and the next `GET device` is 401.
  - `a_subprotocol_token_needs_the_switchboard_name`: `bearer.<token>`
    alone is 401. The existing `subscribe_at` (`:1960`) still upgrades
    with no protocol echoed.
- **`src/adapters/remote.rs` unit test**, beside
  `a_request_reads_with_its_query_bearer_and_body` (`:1045`):
  `a_request_takes_its_bearer_from_the_websocket_protocol`. A header
  bearer wins. Protocols without `switchboard.v1` leave `bearer` empty.
- **`src/core/tests.rs`:** `invite_url_carries_the_code_key_and_id`,
  which checks the exact string for a fixed identity, code, IPv4 and
  port.
- **`tests/ui.rs`:** `remote_devices_dialog_opens_pairing_and_revokes_a_device`
  (`:7424`) parses the copied invite as a URL instead of JSON
  (`:7486-7492`): `https`, `code`, `key` equal to the identity's key,
  `id`. It also finds the browser trust line by label.
- **Swift** (`client/Tests/SwitchboardClientCoreTests/PairingTests.swift`):
  a URL invite parses to one address, and the JSON still parses. Run
  with `(cd client && swift test)`. It is not in CI or the hook.
- Fixtures do not change: no view changed shape.
- Acceptance by hand, recorded in the design status bullet:
  1. Run an instance on a test data dir with script lines
     `remote-listen lan <port>` and `pairing <code>`.
  2. Scan with an iPhone and accept the warning.
  3. Note whether the page is live or polling, and whether the console
     shows a CSP violation.
  4. Start a session waiting and watch it move to the top.
  5. Send a reply.
  6. Revoke the phone and see the page say so.

I accepted all six points and edited the review copy of the plan; the earlier plan is untouched. I re-read the review copy afterwards and every edit is there. The response names the section changed for each point.

1. **Watch set:** excerpts are now limited to the first 8 waiting Claude Code rows. They are fetched only when the page loads and when that session reports a change. Since every content key read in the last minute counts toward the 128-key watch set, the page now takes at most 9 keys (8 excerpts plus the open view), and the plan says so. The design.md text says the same.
2. **A 401 on the socket upgrade:** a browser script can't see the upgrade's status. So after any socket failure or close, the page asks the host who it is (`GET device`):
   - a 401 means it was revoked;
   - a network error means back off and try again, without counting a failure;
   - a 200 counts one failure toward falling back to polling.

   While polling, the page retries the socket once a minute, so a host relaunch doesn't leave it polling for good. The revocation step in the end-to-end test is reworded to match.
3. **The 404's headers:** the 404 and the page files now share a new writer that sends `Connection: close`. The 404 is JSON with none of the page headers, and the test checks exactly that.
4. **The refusal log:** the 404 on the connection thread now logs method and path, as the frame does today. The query is not part of the logged path, so a pairing code is never logged. The spec's §4.1 says so.
5. **CSP and `wss`:** "unverified" is gone. The plan now cites CSP Level 3 and WebKit bug 235873. The fallback only covers WebKit older than April 2022, and a bare `wss:` is ruled out because it would allow any host.
6. **Wrong "Settled" citations and missing spec lines:** the `localStorage` claim now cites the HTML standard instead of the facts file. If the browser won't keep the pairing (a private window, say), the page keeps the token for that tab and says so. The spec lines to amend now include `:309`'s last sentence, `:313` and `:317`.

# Plan feedback, round 2

## Earlier points

1. Watch set: settled. Excerpts are capped at 8 rows, fetched on load and on that session's own `changed`, and the 9-key cost is stated with `:254` cited (plan lines 29-39, 353-370).
2. A 401 on the upgrade: settled. Any socket failure is followed by one `GET device`, which tells revoked (401), unreachable (network error) and a fallback failure (200) apart, and the page retries the socket once a minute while polling (lines 122-137, 375-380, 424-425).
3. The 404's `Connection` header: settled. `respond_closing` writes `Connection: close` for both the page files and the 404, and the test names the exact headers (lines 237-245, 399-400).
4. Refusal log: settled. The connection thread logs method and path only, the query is never logged (the path field excludes it, `src/adapters/remote.rs:362-363`, checked), and the §4.1 doc rule is added (lines 232-233, 246-250, 457-459).
5. CSP `'self'`/`wss`: settled. CSP3 §6.7.2.8 and WebKit bug 235873 are cited, the `wss://<Host>` fallback is limited to WebKit older than April 2022, and a bare `wss:` is ruled out (lines 265-275).
6. Citations and §5 lines: settled. The HTML standard's `WindowLocalStorage` IDL is cited, the case where `localStorage` throws `SecurityError` is handled, and `:309`, `:313` and `:317` are named (lines 174-182, 471-478).

## Cuts

### Where this departs from the issue
- Lines 40-42 ("If the owner wants every row excerpted, a later issue adds…") and lines 55-56 ("Recording revoked hashes would be new host state…"): work this cut does not do. An implementer doesn't need either.
- Lines 72-76, "Facts correction": the plan does not reissue the certificate, so nothing here is built on those lines.

### The record
- Lines 85-88, Decision 6's hypothetical `kind` field: describes a field that is not added. "No change; a browser is a `PairedDevice` named by its `device_name`" is enough.

### The signals
- A section with nothing to say. The one new input, the subprotocol token, is fully specified in Actions 2. Drop the section.

### The actions and effects
- 1, lines 107-114 (why not install the certificate) and 143-144 (the follow-up issue if `fetch` fails): rationale for a path not built.
- 2, lines 166-167: repeats facts `:13`/`:15` and the Commit section's "outside the contract".
- 2, lines 168-173, "Why not the cookie": rejected alternative.
- 2, lines 190-193, the optional `Origin` check "if the owner wants it": machinery for an option not taken.
- 3, lines 208-212, the `.local` alternative: keep at most "IP, because `.local` resolution is Unresolved"; the rest describes a change not made.
- 5, lines 300-302, the `/pair`-scope fallback: a second mechanism where `GET device`, which this plan builds, already suffices.
- 5, line 298, "Spec §4.3 lists it": repeated in Docs (line 460).

### The UI
- Lines 365-370: restate the 9-key account already given at lines 33-39. Keep it in one place.
- Lines 375-380: restate Actions 1's post-failure `GET device` rule. A pointer to Actions 1 is enough.

### The tests
- Line 401, "The existing `/other` check (`:465`) still passes", and lines 427-428, "The existing `subscribe_at` (`:1960`) still upgrades…": existing tests force both.
- Line 443, "Fixtures do not change": the fixture tests force it.

### Docs, Commit
- Nothing to cut.
